h: What to bring and where to go next
p: A little planning makes for a smoother day. Pack swimwear, a towel each, flip-flops for walking around and a change of warm clothes for afterwards. Goggles help younger swimmers and anyone who hates splashes in the eyes, and a water bottle is handy because all that climbing up slide steps is thirsty work. Lockers keep valuables safe, so you can relax and focus on the fun.

Book ahead if you can, particularly in the school holidays and at weekends, and make sure you've chosen a session where the giant slides are running if they're the main attraction for your group. Check height restrictions as a family before you go so there are no tears at the top of the stairs.
How long to allow? Your session will set the pace, but arrive early enough to get changed and make the most of your time. Younger children will appreciate a break and a snack halfway through.

Coral Reef sits right on the edge of some lovely countryside. Right next door is The Look Out Discovery Centre, a hands-on science centre with lots of interactive exhibits that makes a great add-on for curious kids. Swinley Forest, on the doorstep, has miles of trails for walking and cycling, and Go Ape offers treetop adventures for older children and adults.

In town, The Lexicon shopping centre has plenty of shops and places to eat if you fancy a bite after your swim. Windsor, with its famous castle and riverside walks, is a short drive away, and so is Legoland Windsor if you're planning a bigger family weekend.
